text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The high court is to rule on Tuesday whether the state can use as part of its appeal against the acquittal of former president Kamuzu Banda, part of the preliminary hearing of the trial in which Banda was accused of plotting to murder three politicians in 1983.
- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) confirmed on Monday it had met President Bakili Muluzi in Lilongwe on Friday to end the country's political impasse.
- Agriculture experts have dismissed fears that heavy rains could destroy this year's maize crop production and lead to famine.

- Malawi's foreign exchange earnings could drop this year if heavy rains persist affecting the quality of tobacco, which last year accounted for 86 percent of forex earnings, a tobacco researcher said.
- A Yugoslav woman, who claims to see visions of Mary, Mother of Jesus Christ in Madjugorje, on Sunday drew thousands of Catholic believers in Blantyre to hear her message.
